intro.text: Guided by a belief in the power of next, AMSC is a leading provider of power controls solutions that apply innovation and creativity to address today's challenges and enable a more resilient and sustainable energy future. Driven by the purpose "to power progress," the Company integrates future-facing technologies to balance the global demand for clean energy with reliable, efficient power delivery. AMSC delivers advanced grid systems and engineering services to optimize network reliability, provides ship protection and power management solutions to enhance fleet efficiency and safety, and supplies electronic controls and designs that reduce wind energy costs. Beyond these systems, the Company provides capabilities in industrial process and control alongside environmental and emission control to ensure operational efficiency across the entire energy infrastructure.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In fiscal 2025, Inox accounted for 15% and Fuji Bridex accounted for 10% of our total revenues.
In fiscal 2024, Inox accounted for 14% of our total revenues.
In fiscal 2023, Inox accounted for 13% of our total revenues.
No other customer accounted for more than 10% of our total revenues in each of fiscal 2025, 2024, and 2023.
In addition, approximately 16% and 7% of our revenues in fiscal 2025 were derived under sales contracts where prices were denominated in the Euro and Real, respectively.
The Grid business segment accounted for 84% of total revenues in both fiscal 2025 and 2024.
Our Wind business segment accounted for 16% of total revenues in both fiscal 2025 and 2024.
For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 , 89 % of revenue was recognized at the point in time when control transferred to the customer, with the remainder being recognized over time.
For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025 , 88 % of revenue was recognized at the point in time when control transferred to the customer, with the remainder being recognized over time.
For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2024 , 80 % of revenue was recognized at the point in time when control transferred to the customer, with the remainder being recognized over time.

This exciting energy future also depends on computer chips, batteries and fuel cells that are built from silicon, lithium and carbon.

We believe that competitive performance in the marketplace depends upon several factors, including technical innovation, range of products and services, product quality and reliability, customer service and technical support.

We rely upon third-party suppliers for the components and subassemblies of many of our Grid and Wind products, making us vulnerable to supply shortages and price fluctuations, which could harm our business.
Many of our components and subassemblies are currently manufactured for us by a limited number of qualified suppliers.

We rely upon the capacity, reliability, and security of information technology hardware and software infrastructure and networks (collectively, "IT Systems"), and our ability to expand and update such IT Systems in response to our changing needs.
We manage certain IT Systems but also rely on IT Systems and various products and services provided by critical third-party vendors and others in the supply chain.

Because we rely on certain third party vendors that support our operations, successful cyberattacks that disrupt or result in unauthorized access to third-party IT Systems can materially impact our operations and financial results.
While we achieved profitable results in fiscal 2025 and 2024, our ability to sustain profitability depends on numerous factors, many of which are outside of our control.

As a result of all of these factors, comparing our operating results on a period-to-period basis may not be meaningful, and you should not rely on our past results as an indication of our future performance.

We have operations in, and depend on sales in, emerging markets, including Latin America and India, and global conditions could negatively affect our operating results or limit our ability to expand our operations outside of these markets.
Our financial performance depends upon our ability to carry on our operations and sell our products in such emerging markets.
The success of our business will also depend on our ability to develop new technologies without infringing or misappropriating the proprietary rights of others.
We rely on trade secrets to protect the majority of our proprietary technologies, especially where we do not believe patent protection is appropriate or obtainable.
We also rely on trade secrets and proprietary know-how to protect our intellectual property.

Our business, like others within the energy technologies industry, is faced with growing cybersecurity threats as we increasingly rely on digital technologies across our business, some of which are managed by third -party service providers on whom we rely to help us collect, host or process information.
The Company’s primary sources of liquidity are internally generated cash provided by operating activities, our cash and cash equivalents on hand, along with access to capital markets.

We have a long history of working with multiple types of projects and preparing cost estimates, and we rely on the expertise of key personnel to prepare what we believe are reasonable best estimates given available facts and circumstances.
